goal_title: Book: Vectors & Forces: From Direction to Dynamics — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in forces became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note

book.title: Vectors & Forces: From Direction to Dynamics
chapters_read: Flow_Field (last hall of change, handover in)
FormFinding_Descent (first hall of formfinding, handover out)

reading.arc: Forces takes a vector from a portable difference between two pins to a rule that owns the visitor's own locomotion. The first three halls build the arithmetic (displacement, sum, gap, projection, cross product) as relations that describe and do not push; Launch and Motion admit time, first as a closed-form curve and then as a rigid body that keeps its velocity after the command ends; Fields and Kinetic Forces ask what a receiver does with a sampled arrow (replace or accumulate; drag, nominal work, a prescribed circle). Oscillation and Choreography show returning and shared clocks; Gravity, Legs and Arena move from a held centre to mutual attraction, from prescribed gait to contact and support, and to what an encounter shares; Force as Place finally lets the visitor enter the sentence, with a plank kept beside the crossing. The sequence's refrain is the truth line in forces.json: an arrow does not decide, its quantity, frame, receiver and retained state do. Every tagged work resolves to a scene and every map token carries the #lesson config the chapter describes, so the encounters are real; the defects are in the prose and the joins.
holds: The receiver question, asked at every console: what does this vector measure, and what does the receiving body do with it (= versus +=, apply_central_force versus a prescribed path versus a controller handoff).
The retained state: something acquired earlier keeps crossing the room, from the one-second pulse in Motion to the spring crossing its line to the velocity carried into the field in Act5.
One console grammar throughout: PARTS then RULE, RESET semantics spelled out, the gold or amber perimeter that ends an observation rather than doing work, and 'the museum's clock is elsewhere'.
A carried vocabulary: amber A, pink B, cyan result; X across and F forward; a floor plan turned upright on the wall that never authorizes a climb.
Two kinds of body in every hall: the visitor walks through drawings while divided from them by collision layers, until Act5 admits the visitor as a receiver.
Each hall closes by naming the next and opens by recalling the last, which makes the one missing join (Choreography to Gravity) audible.

hall_notes.note: Two benches: a hand-sized arrow projected twice on the wall (SHORT, LONG, SHIFT, ZERO, PARTS), then the normaliser with its 0.001 threshold. Tight and clear about reuse coming from discarding; it ends by naming the next hall with its file ID.

One machine, the adder board with a carriage, makes addition a journey: SWAP moves the corner, PATH removes it, CANCEL sends the cube out and back to a zero sum. The best-paced hall in the sequence; the zero-is-not-nothing turn lands.

Five works in a row (add pads, subtraction stage, aligner, projection wall, torque crank). Dense but disciplined; the projection station reading the subtraction station's live gap is the highlight, and the aligner and crank are honestly framed as diagrams with limits.

A room-scale analytic projectile with the complementary launch in the lane behind you. Reads as an invitation to stand between two flights; the reset and resolution paragraphs near the end run long but every number checks.

The hinge of the sequence: a rigid body keeps velocity after a one-second pulse, COAST against BRAKE against DRAG, then the friction ramp's threshold. Careful about what the engine does and what the script does, and compares the two implementations without flattering either.

Cyan replaces velocity, pink accumulates; the same field, two receivers; SWIRL, UNIFORM, REVERSE. The clearest statement of the sequence's thesis; the step-and-sample paragraph near the end reads as a datasheet.

The drag corridor (three coefficients, one rule, a walk-through passage), the mower's signed work against path against cut grass, and the prescribed centrifuge. Strong on same look, different mechanism; carries the sequence's one desktop aside.

The spring cube crosses its line; DAMP names tied to mass and stiffness; what the grab discards. Thoughtful about the word restoring, defers the rest to Wavefunctions and points cleanly to the timing machines.
Twenty rotors (offset, wave, drift) and a conveyor whose backlog is a physical heap. The most playful voice in the sequence; the only hall that ends without a pointer to the next.

A held source and a free satellite (REVERSE retraces), then mutual bodies, a third body and a nudged copy with an RMS readout. Precise about what the edge and the trail cannot prove; the opener reaches back to the spring rather than to the hall just left.

The support polygon lab (posts, hull, shifted load, release) set against seven prescribed walkers. The plate-versus-walker contrast is the sequence's best argument about permissions, and the width-of-a-foot paragraph is a small revelation.

A scoped crab choosing between a mushroom and a nominated visitor (you), a sight line, five meals to rooted; then the collision-carts diagram. Two halves of unequal weight, the second a console diagram after a live encounter.

Aim a local acceleration (with the idle yaw at the pole made visible), test it on a cube, then enter it; the plank stays. The hall where the visitor becomes a receiver; its field paragraph still describes the desktop walker.

stumbles: Vectors_Act1_WhatAVectorIs: the closing pointer prints a file name: 'Next, in VFM_02_Operations, vectors meet.'
Change_Choreography: the only hall with no closing pointer; VFM_07_Gravity then opens 'The spring had an address to return to', reaching back two halls past the rods and the conveyor.
Vectors_Act4a_KineticForces: 'The same desktop movement command carries you progressively less quickly' addresses a visitor who has no desktop command in the headset.
Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace: 'Ordinary keyboard or stick steering' and 'the desktop walker returns horizontal movement' describe the test rig, not the visitor's body.
Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace: the only chapter without a title line after twelve titled halls; the first sentence reads as a heading and then continues as prose.
Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace: 'The last slider stops at fifteen' carries no unit, and 'becomes the most powerful control on the console' overstates what yaw does just off the pole.
VFM_02_Operations: 'Its body is possible within this particular translation between representations' leaves the reader unsure whose body and what is being permitted.
Flow_Field into Vectors_Act1: the previous sequence promises a push that ends while the cube keeps going; the bench that follows measures pins, and the push is four halls away.

Vectors_Act3_FieldsAndMotion (also Motion, Oscillation, Gravity): the closing limits paragraph, stall cap, sample count, frame exit, repeats in the same order each hall, and by the fourth reading it is a datasheet.
VFM_08_Arena: one H2 ('What the collision shares') for the second work and none for the first, so the heading reads as if it names the whole hall.

keep.quote: Zero has not meant that nothing happened.
The command lasts one second. The cube keeps going.
An equals sign and a plus-equals sign give the same spatial rule different consequences.
Here we have established a smaller thing to carry: a force can bring a body back without telling it to stop there.
A reference need not be occupied.
Its empty-looking interior is full of decisions.
How quickly might we have called this trust, taming, exhaustion, or friendship if the counter and the code had stayed hidden?
We have learned to look for the place where an instruction becomes a consequence.

reading.handover_in: Flow_Field closes 'In Forces, a push will end and a cube will keep going. Something it received earlier will still be crossing the room.' Vectors_Act1 opens with a recap ('given points addresses, transformed shapes, made patterns and followed changes through time') and the question 'Can something move without its vector changing?', then measures pins. The promise is kept, but only at VFM_03_Motion, hall 5 of 13; Act1 neither picks it up nor defers it, so the visitor arrives expecting motion and gets a bench. Loose, not broken.
reading.handover_out: Vectors_Act5 closes 'In the next sequence, Form Finding, that question reaches the shape of the world itself', and FormFinding_Descent opens 'The last room let a field carry you across a gap. You brought motion into it; the field changed that motion; something of the journey remained when you left', then states the break outright: 'This is already a departure from Forces. There is no stored velocity here.' A clean join. One note for the next sequence's own pass: Descent line 39, 'In the recorded desktop comparison', is a desktop aside in reader prose.

tasks.title: Name Newton's three laws where the halls perform them: the push that keeps going, MASS, and mutual = false

NOC states all three (its version of the third - forces occur in pairs, on different objects, the truck on ice, the roller skates - is the cleanest around). Thirteen halls, and neither Newton nor Aristotle is named.

Footnote: Isaac Newton, Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (1687), the three laws of motion; Aristotle, Physics, on forced motion.

tasks.proposal: After the pink rule: 'Hold on to the difference. In Randomness, the beads in a glass tank will replace their velocity with a new draw at every step, and jitter; a body that adds its draws to what it already has, as pink does, glides. The same rule, received two ways.'
